title: Henri Coanda's patent and Project Y at Wright-Patterson
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Henri Coanda's patent and Project Y at Wright-Patterson, about 1936 onward at Vichy France; Wright-Patterson AFB, Ohio, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of Henri Coanda, a Romanian scientist who he says held a patent from 1936 on a flight technology and was living in Vichy France, the French state under Nazi influence during the war. According to Michels, Coanda was forced to work for the Nazis and was later taken to Wright-Patterson, a US Air Force base in Ohio, to work on Project Y. Michels says Project Y grew out of the Avro car project, an effort to make flying saucers actually fly, which would mean the US was quietly building saucer craft after the war.
